messages:
marco (docs): Hey team, quick catch: the API reference for /v1/classify shows a `response_format` enum with values `text` and `json`, but the runtime actually expects `plain_text` and `application_json`. The mismatch is causing the Python SDK example to set `response_format='text'` and get a 400.

isla (sdk): Oof. Which file and snippet? I can patch the SDK helpers and examples.

marco (docs): docs/reference/classify.md, the examples use `response_format: json` in curl and `response_format='text'` in the Python snippet. Server validation rejects `text`.

arun (api): Confirmed on the API side. We standardized the enum to match HTTP media types to reduce ambiguity: `plain_text` and `application_json` (we kept short aliasing in the catalog but not the strict validator). The validator is strict for public endpoints now. This change slipped through docs.

emma (pm): Is this a breaking change for users who depended on `text`? Any telemetry on how many requests use the old values?

arun (api): We saw a small number of legacy calls but most SDKs used the alias mapping. We turned on strict validation in the last deploy to prevent downstream ambiguity (content-type parsing). So it's mostly a docs + examples mismatch.

marco (docs): Proposed doc fix: 1) Update the enum table to list canonical values `plain_text` and `application_json` with a short column: "legacy aliases: `text` -> `plain_text`, `json` -> `application_json` (deprecated)". 2) Update all examples (curl, Node, Python) to use canonical values. 3) Add a migration note and a short SDK snippet showing how to map old values to new ones.

isla (sdk): I'll add a helper in the SDK: `normalize_response_format(value)` that maps aliases to canonical values and logs a deprecation warning. Also update the Python example to use `response_format='plain_text'`. I'll open a combined docs+sdk PR so they land together.

ci-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/900 by isla (sdk)  runs: lint, linkcheck, example-tests.

arun (api): Note for docs: when both alias and canonical are supplied, runtime prefers canonical. If alias is supplied and no canonical provided, acceptance depends on validator flags; best practice is to use canonical. Please add that to the behavior notes.

emma (pm): Add a short line to release notes about clarifying enum names and SDK deprecation helper. We should avoid calling this "breaking" but do call out strict validation rollout.

isla (sdk): PR includes: updated docs/reference/classify.md (enum table + examples), updated examples/python/classify_example.py, added SDK helper normalize_response_format with a small unit test, and a tiny deprecation log message. Preview: https://deploy-preview.docs.redwood.ai/900/reference/classify.html

ci-bot: docs lint found a style nit in the enum table. isla (sdk) pushed fix.

ci-bot: All checks passed for PR #900.

isla (sdk): Merged. @marco please add the release-note blurb; @emma can you sign off on PM messaging?

marco (docs): Draft blurb: "Docs: clarified `response_format` values for /v1/classify. Use `plain_text` or `application_json` (aliases `text` and `json` are deprecated). SDKs now include a helper to normalize legacy aliases."

emma (pm): LGTM. Let's add a short note in the weekly customer email for integrators who parse raw responses.

marco (docs): Done. Closing thread 44b
